nodes.label: Advanced AI accelerator
nodes.what: A high-performance compute package combining logic dies, HBM and advanced packaging for AI systems.
nodes.why_matters: Anchor product. Its shipment rate depends on a coupled memory, packaging, substrate, test and power chain.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls qualified HBM, advanced packaging starts, interposers, substrates, test capacity and data-center power.

nodes.label: HBM3E
nodes.what: High-bandwidth memory stacks attached to current AI accelerator packages.
nodes.why_matters: A package cannot ship without enough qualified memory stacks.
nodes.if_scales: Increases demand for DRAM wafers, stacking, bonding and memory test.

nodes.label: HBM4
nodes.what: Next-generation high-bandwidth memory with wider interfaces and higher bandwidth per stack.
nodes.why_matters: Next-generation accelerator platforms are designed around qualified HBM4 supply.
nodes.if_scales: Moves demand toward HBM4 wafer, stacking and qualification capacity.

nodes.label: Logic-wafer fabrication
nodes.what: Leading-edge wafer fabrication for accelerator logic dies.
nodes.why_matters: The compute die is the central silicon input before package assembly.
nodes.if_scales: Raises leading-edge wafer starts and advanced process qualification demand.

nodes.label: CoWoS-class advanced packaging
nodes.what: 2.5D package assembly attaching logic and HBM on an interposer.
nodes.why_matters: The package-level integration step determines whether separate dies become a shippable accelerator.
nodes.if_scales: Increases advanced-packaging starts, tools, substrates and package-test demand.

nodes.label: Advanced interposer
nodes.what: Silicon or redistribution-layer carrier for dense die-to-die and HBM connections.
nodes.why_matters: Interposer area and yield constrain how many HBM stacks fit in a package.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls interposer wafer, lithography, bonding and inspection capacity.

nodes.label: Package substrate
nodes.what: Large multilayer substrate connecting the assembled package to the board or system.
nodes.why_matters: Large AI packages require high-layer-count substrates with suitable yield.
nodes.if_scales: Increases substrate starts and qualification with advanced-package customers.

nodes.label: HBM stacking and bonding
nodes.what: Assembly of DRAM dies into tested memory stacks using TSV and bonding processes.
nodes.why_matters: Stack height and yield determine usable memory bits per package footprint.
nodes.if_scales: Raises demand for bonding tools, assembly capacity and known-good-die screening.

nodes.label: Package and system test
nodes.what: Electrical, thermal and reliability testing of completed multi-die accelerator packages.
nodes.why_matters: Test throughput is required before assembled packages can enter systems.
nodes.if_scales: Increases ATE, burn-in, thermal handling and parallel-test requirements.

nodes.label: Hybrid-bonding equipment
nodes.what: Equipment used for dense copper-to-copper or hybrid-bonded die and stack assembly.
nodes.why_matters: Shared bonding tool capacity can serve multiple advanced memory and 3D packaging flows.
nodes.if_scales: Makes tool install rate, yield and service capacity more important to package output.

nodes.label: HBM memory suppliers
nodes.what: Qualified memory manufacturers supplying HBM3E and HBM4 stacks.
nodes.why_matters: The qualified supplier set is narrower than ordinary DRAM supply.
nodes.if_scales: Concentrates qualification, allocation and ramp exposure among a small supplier group.

nodes.label: TSMC
nodes.what: Foundry and advanced-packaging provider with CoWoS-class and related package flows.
nodes.why_matters: A named provider in the dominant advanced accelerator manufacturing path.
nodes.if_scales: Its packaging allocation and expansion pace influence completed accelerator output.

nodes.label: Advanced-packaging tool suppliers
nodes.what: Providers of bonding, lithography, inspection and assembly equipment used in advanced packages.
nodes.why_matters: Tool availability and process maturity affect effective package capacity.
nodes.if_scales: Tool lead times and shared-factory demand can shape packaging expansion speed.

nodes.label: AI server system
nodes.what: Server platform that integrates accelerator packages, networking, storage and power delivery.
nodes.why_matters: Accelerator demand is realized only when packages can be qualified in complete systems.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls boards, thermal systems, networking, rack integration and acceptance testing.

nodes.label: Data-center power and cooling
nodes.what: Electrical service, power distribution and thermal management supporting AI server deployment.
nodes.why_matters: A shipped accelerator still needs deployable rack power and cooling capacity.
nodes.if_scales: Raises demand for grid interconnects, power equipment, cooling and site commissioning.

nodes.label: AI cluster capacity
nodes.what: Connected fleet of AI servers operating as a training or inference cluster.
nodes.why_matters: Cluster availability converts individual accelerator supply into usable compute capacity.
nodes.if_scales: Pulls networking, facilities, operations and power beyond the package boundary.

nodes.label: Advanced-packaging production geography
nodes.what: The locations where qualified advanced packaging and associated test capacity are installed.
nodes.why_matters: A concentrated geography can expose the chain to local power, logistics or disruption risk.
nodes.if_scales: Expansion requires permits, utilities, skilled labor and resilient logistics at selected sites.
